description: Brainograph shared kernel (rewrite, v2): frozen platform wire contracts (response envelope, DataProvider models/executor, entity bases, permission/role enums), JWT authentication, the exception-to-envelope map, and the envelope-typed BaseApiClient.
releaseNotes:
6.53.0 — ADDITIVE: TWO new ApplicationAdminPermission members, 244-245, ViewFeedbackSuggestions / TriageFeedbackSuggestions (BG-112 AC-3: the bg-feedback suggestions inbox was gated by an admin role alone). Appended, so ordinals 1-243 are unchanged; the committed permission catalogue is regenerated. No behaviour change in this package: bg-feedback starts requiring them only after its own re-pin, and bg-identity grants them to the admin roles (seed plus a backfill for existing holders) BEFORE that. Existing principals receive no personal grant because the enum grew. SuperAdmin passes every [HasPermission] without a grant (6.17.0).

6.52.0 — ADDITIVE: one service scope (GEN-ADR-1, BG-1560, the co-working invitations). New: ServiceScopes.IdentityUserDirectoryRead = "identity.userdirectory.read", audience https://identity.api/ (READ-ONLY; bg-usercontent finds ONE user by exact e-mail or phone and reads display names of known ids; id, display name and avatar only, never e-mail or phone). Owner, 2026-10-29 15:40 CST, typed in the performing session's window (dev 2): «Q1 да, один scope; Q2 да». No audience is added; no behaviour change for any scope declared earlier. A client holds the scope only once bg-identity grants it (svc-usercontent; a separate additive change).

6.51.0 — ADDITIVE: two service scopes and one receiver audience (GEN-ADR-1, BG-1518). New: ServiceScopes.IdentityLearningDimensionsRead = "identity.learningdimensions.read", audience https://identity.api/ (READ-ONLY; bg-aiagent reads one learner's dimension ids - country, region, school, grade, user type; no names, no birth year). ServiceScopes.AnalyticLearningIngest = "analytic.learning.ingest", audience https://analytic.api/ (a WRITE scope; bg-aiagent delivers anonymous learning deltas, no user id). ServiceTokens startup now accepts the analytic audience; before, ServiceTokens:Audience https://analytic.api/ was refused as "not a service audience". Owner, 2026-10-29 ~06:49Z, typed in the performing session's window: «да, оба scope: identity.learningdimensions.read и analytic.learning.ingest для svc-aiagent» (ADR 0002 Amendment 2026-10-29). No behaviour change for any scope declared earlier. A client holds a scope only once bg-identity grants it. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (a new authorization surface).

6.50.0 — BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (BG-1442): BaseApiClient no longer copies the inbound request's Authorization header onto the outbound call; services talk with service tokens, never a forwarded user bearer (owner rule 2026-09-27). A client now sends no credential until its subclass supplies one (ApplyServiceAuthorizationAsync or its own header). The 6.49.0 constructor flag forwardInboundAuthorization stays: false (what the five known clients pass) is unchanged; true now throws ArgumentException instead of being ignored. A consumer that took 6.49.0 or earlier AND relied on the copy (the fleet census found only usercontent's invite mailer, since removed) loses its Authorization on this version.

6.49.0 — ADDITIVE: BaseApiClient can be told NOT to forward the inbound bearer (BG-1442). New protected constructor BaseApiClient(IHttpClientFactory, IHttpContextAccessor, ILoggerFactory?, bool forwardInboundAuthorization); false copies no Authorization header from the ambient request. The default is UNCHANGED (true): the three existing constructors behave exactly as before, so no consumer changes behaviour by taking this version. A later release flips the default once nothing relies on the copy.

6.48.0 — ADDITIVE: one service scope and one receiver audience for bg-media (GEN-ADR-1, BG-1412). New: ServiceScopes.MediaContentUrlRead = "media.content.url.read", audience https://media.api/ (READ-ONLY; bg-feedback resolves the delivery URL of a reporter's private screenshot with its own service token instead of forwarding the staff user's bearer). The acting user in the token is the asset's OWNER (the reporter), not the person who clicked; the receiver admits only when the asset's OwnerId equals it. ServiceTokens startup now accepts the media audience; before, ServiceTokens:Audience https://media.api/ was refused as "not a service audience". Owner, 2026-10-26 05:55:25Z, typed in the performing session's window: «А» (ADR 0002 Amendment 2026-10-26, second). No behaviour change for any scope declared earlier. A client holds it only once bg-identity grants it. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (a new authorization surface).

6.47.0 — ADDITIVE: one service scope and one receiver audience for bg-aiagent (GEN-ADR-1, BG-1410). New: ServiceScopes.AiAgentIntakeClassify = "aiagent.intake.classify", audience https://aiagent.api/ (NOT a write scope; bg-feedback asks the intake classifier with its own service token naming the acting user and the request, instead of forwarding the end user's bearer). ServiceTokens startup now accepts the aiagent audience; before, ServiceTokens:Audience https://aiagent.api/ was refused as "not a service audience". Owner, 2026-10-26 04:10Z, typed in the performing session's window: «Хорошо, я согласен с твоим советом, делай так» (ADR 0002 Amendment 2026-10-26). No behaviour change for any scope declared earlier. A client holds it only once bg-identity grants it. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (a new authorization surface).

6.46.0 — ADDITIVE, OFF BY DEFAULT: session revocation (BG-1338). SessionRevocation:Enabled (default false) polls bg-identity (GET api/Session/Ended, a SERVICE token, every 5 s) and refuses a user token issued at or before its owner's sessions ended: 401, error_description=session_ended (code auth.session.ended). Also ServiceScopes.IdentitySessionsRead = "identity.sessions.read", audience https://identity.api/ (READ-ONLY; owner typed yes 2026-10-23). Disabled the registration is exactly the 6.45.0 one. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone.

6.45.0 — ADDITIVE: one service scope and one receiver audience for bg-identity (GEN-ADR-1). New: ServiceScopes.IdentitySchoolUserStatsRead = "identity.schooluserstats.read", audience https://identity.api/ (READ-ONLY, counts only; bg-dictionary reads the school-user aggregate with it instead of forwarding the admin's bearer, bg-dictionary#21). ServiceTokens startup now accepts the identity audience; before, ServiceTokens:Audience https://identity.api/ was refused as "not a service audience". Owner, 2026-10-14 17:41 CST, typed in the performing session's window: «да» (ADR 0002 Amendment 2026-10-14, third). No behaviour change for any scope declared earlier. An endpoint uses the scope by declaring [AllowServiceScope]; a client holds it only once bg-identity grants it (the svc-dictionary client is a separate, additive change). Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (a new authorization surface).

6.44.0 — BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (mechanism, no new right): an action may declare MORE THAN ONE [AllowServiceScope] and admission is ANY-OF (GEN-ADR-1; owner rule 2026-10-05 'every endpoint accepts a service token'; coordinator decision 2026-10-14). AllowServiceScopeAttribute is now repeatable: a service token is admitted when it holds ANY declared scope that belongs to this receiver's audience; a declared scope of another receiver's audience admits nothing; with ONE attribute behaviour is exactly as before. New: ClaimsPrincipal.HasServiceScope(scope) (the service-authenticated token HOLDS the scope) and HttpContext.WasAdmittedUnderServiceScope(scope) (the call was admitted under it: the matched endpoint declares it, it belongs to this audience, the token holds it) - a receiver that branches on what a caller may see uses the second. The user-gate bypass (a scope on a [HasPermission] or role-gated action replaces that gate for its holder, since 6.27.0) applies to every declared scope alike. WHAT A RE-PIN CARRIES: the attribute is inherited and repeatable, so a derived override's attribute is ADDED to the base action's where it used to REPLACE it (no consumer overrides an action today; one that does must restate the scopes it means). A consumer test that reads the attribute with GetMetadata (single) silently picks the last of several; read them with GetOrderedMetadata. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (an authentication surface).

6.43.0 — ADDITIVE: two WRITE service scopes for acting-user writes (GEN-ADR-1, ADR 0002 Amendment 2026-10-14; bg-shared#27). New: ServiceScopes.ContentWriteAsUser = "content.writeasuser" (audience https://content.api/) and ServiceScopes.UserContentWriteAsUser = "usercontent.writeasuser" (audience https://usercontent.api/); both are in the known-scope list and in the scope-to-audience table, so [AllowServiceScope] with either is admitted by the kernel on the right host. Write scopes: requested ALONE. A receiver that declares one is expected to take the owner from GetActingUserId() and to refuse a call without it; the kernel enforces neither. No behaviour change for any scope declared earlier or for any receiver that does not declare these. A client holds a scope only once bg-identity registers and grants it (a separate change). Names confirmed by the owner 2026-10-14 (relayed through the coordinator); the ADR matrix row is a separate amendment. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (a new authorization surface).

6.42.0 — ADDITIVE: the acting user and the request id on a SERVICE token (GEN-ADR-1, ADR 0002 Amendments 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-14; bg-shared#27). New: ServiceTokenClaims.ActingUser = "bg_acting_user" and ServiceTokenClaims.RequestId = "bg_request_id"; ClaimsPrincipal.GetActingUserId() / GetRequestId(), which answer ONLY for a principal the SERVICE handler authenticated (a user token carrying the same claim names yields null); ActingServiceTokenProvider (one token per acting user and request, bounded cache, single-flight, ArgumentException before any request on a malformed context) and AddActingServiceTokenProvider (singleton). Behaviour change on the receiving side: a service token with a duplicated, malformed or half-stated acting context (an acting user without a request id) is now REFUSED; a token without the claims is unchanged. The claims are ATTRIBUTION ONLY (owner, B3): they add no authority, and the refusal of sid, roles, permissions and job claims is unchanged. bg-identity does not stamp them yet (its per-client right and the mint are a separate change), so no token carries them until then. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (an authentication surface).

6.41.0 — ADDITIVE: one service scope for bg-gis -> bg-content (GEN-ADR-1). New: ServiceScopes.ContentBaseMapUsageRead = "content.basemap.usage.read", audience https://content.api/ (the audience content already has; READ-ONLY, COUNTS only: bg-gis asks who uses a base map - lessons and education folders - before it trashes or purges one, G5-extra). Owner, 2026-10-06 15:53 CST, typed: «да, разрешаю G5-extra: правку ADR 0002 и GEN-AUTH.md» (ADR 0002 and dev-kit GEN-AUTH.md carry the row). No behaviour change for any scope declared earlier. A client holds the scope only once bg-identity grants it (the svc-gis client is a separate, additive change); a receiver uses it by declaring [AllowServiceScope] on the usage action only. Adopt by a pin move; ships alone (a new authorization surface).

6.40.0 — ADDITIVE: one service scope and one receiver audience for bg-dictionary (GEN-ADR-1). New: ServiceScopes.DictionarySubjectSettingRead = "dictionary.subjectsetting.read", audience https://dictionary.api/ (READ-ONLY; bg-content#103 reads the main base map of a subject with it). ServiceTokens startup now accepts the dictionary audience; before, ServiceTokens:Audience https://dictionary.api/ was refused as "not a service audience". Owner, 2026-10-06 13:25 CST, typed: «Да, разрешаю правку ADR 0002 и GEN-AUTH.md» (ADR 0002 and dev-kit GEN-AUTH.md carry the row). No behaviour change for any scope declared before this version; an endpoint uses the scope by declaring [AllowServiceScope], and a client holds it only once bg-identity grants it.

6.39.0 — BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (authorization), no new members: EraseUser LEAVES ExcludedForSuperModerator (owner, 2026-10-06, bg-identity#120: a SuperModerator may erase accounts, except a SuperAdmin or another SuperModerator - that target check is bg-identity’s, read from the database, not this gate). ExcludedForSuperModerator is back to CreateSuperAdminUser, UpdateSuperAdminUser, DeleteSuperAdminUser; a SuperModerator passes a [HasPermission] gate accepting ONLY EraseUser again. Everything else is unchanged from 6.38.0. Consumers must read docs/CHANGELOG.md 6.39.0 before re-pinning.

6.38.0 — BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (authorization), no new members: EraseUser joins ExcludedForSuperModerator (owner, 2026-10-05 17:35: erasing an account is SuperAdmin-only). A SuperModerator no longer passes a [HasPermission] gate accepting ONLY CreateSuperAdminUser, UpdateSuperAdminUser, DeleteSuperAdminUser or EraseUser; everything else is unchanged from 6.37.0. Consumers must read docs/CHANGELOG.md 6.38.0 before re-pinning.

6.37.0 — BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (authorization), no new members: SuperModerator passes every [HasPermission] gate except one whose accepted permissions are ONLY CreateSuperAdminUser, UpdateSuperAdminUser, DeleteSuperAdminUser (owner, 2026-10-05), future members included, with no personal grant. New public PermissionGate (Brainograph.Utilities.Authentication): ExcludedForSuperModerator, RoleBypasses, HasPermissionOrRoleBypass - the one rule the filter and every consumer in-action check should call. SuperAdmin unchanged (passes everything). Consumers must read docs/CHANGELOG.md 6.37.0 before re-pinning.

6.36.0 — ADDITIVE: FOUR new ApplicationAdminPermission members, 240-243, ReadAiQuiz / UpdateAiQuiz / PublishAiQuiz / DeleteAiQuiz (bg-aiagent#72, the admin side of AI-generated quizzes: versions, review, approval before learners see a quiz). APPENDED AT THE END as the freeze contract requires (ordinals 1-239 unchanged; the ordinal IS the bit position in the compact perms claim); ApplicationAdminPermissionFreezeTests was taken RED first. Publish is its own grant, separate from Update. NOT a gate on generation: generation stays open to anyone with a quota, and no UseAi* member is enforced on the quiz routes (the comment that said UseAiTeachingTools gates generation was wrong and is corrected). ALSO: the four FolderLabel members 209-212 are marked [Obsolete] (a warning; bg-content#157, folder labels are removed) and keep their ordinals; a service that still names one in code gets CS0618, an error under TreatWarningsAsErrors, so it re-pins only after it stops naming them. Existing principals receive no personal grant because the enum grew — admins grant them (owner, 2026-10-05); SuperAdmin passes without one. Consumers re-pin to 6.36.0.  PREVIOUSLY, 6.35.0 — BEHAVIOUR: a request ABORTED BY THE CLIENT (HttpContext.RequestAborted cancelled, response not started) is answered 499 with no body and logged ONCE at Information (method and path, no stack) by ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, instead of 500 + Error + Sentry. An OperationCanceledException from an outbound timeout or the service's own token still maps to 500 + Error, unchanged. Amends ERROR-HANDLING section 1 (ratified 2026-07-09) on the owner's typed yes, 2026-10-05: «да, 499». No API surface changed; consumers re-pin to 6.35.0. PREVIOUSLY, 6.34.0 — ADDITIVE: SIX new ApplicationAdminPermission members, 234-239, ReadAuthoredQuiz / CreateAuthoredQuiz / UpdateAuthoredQuiz / DeleteAuthoredQuiz / RestoreAuthoredQuiz / PurgeAuthoredQuiz (bg-content#150, authored quizzes: embed codes with a title per language, shared by lessons and education folders). NOT the AI quizzes of bg-aiagent (UseAiTeachingTools). APPENDED AT THE END as the freeze contract requires: ApplicationAdminPermissionFreezeTests was taken RED first (2 of 2: the count and the name/value collection) and green only after the append; the committed catalogue is REGENERATED, not edited. Learners read Published quizzes through an [Authorize] route that needs no member. Consumers re-pin to 6.34.0; existing principals receive no personal grant from the enum growing - admins grant them (owner rule), and bg-identity adds only the role-map entries. Nothing existing changed. PREVIOUSLY, 6.33.0 — ADDITIVE: TWO new ApplicationAdminPermission members, 232 RestoreUser and 233 EraseUser (bg-identity#113, recoverable account deletion). RestoreUser reverses an administrator soft delete; EraseUser is the irreversible erasure of an already soft-deleted account. APPENDED AT THE END as the freeze contract requires: ApplicationAdminPermissionFreezeTests was taken RED first (2 of 2: the count and the name/value collection) and green only after the append; the committed catalogue is REGENERATED, not edited. Shared owns the names and ordinals; bg-identity owns the default-role distribution. Consumers re-pin to 6.33.0; existing principals receive no personal grant from the enum growing - admins grant them (owner rule). Nothing existing changed. PREVIOUSLY, 6.32.0 — ADDITIVE: TWO new ApplicationAdminPermission members, 230 RestorePresentation and 231 PurgePresentation (bg-usercontent#53). They keep reversible recovery and delete-forever separate from DeletePresentation. Owner decision 2026-09-29: ContentManager receives RestorePresentation but NOT PurgePresentation; SuperAdmin and SuperModerator receive both; no other default role receives either. APPENDED AT THE END so every existing ordinal remains unchanged. The catalogue is regenerated from the enum. Consumers must re-pin; Identity must seed the approved default-role map, while grants for already-assigned principals remain a separately measured and authorized data change. Full prior notes remain in docs/CHANGELOG.md.
